questions.question: Which cloud service type lets developers deploy applications without managing the underlying operating system?

options.why: In IaaS you manage the OS.
Correct. The provider manages the OS, runtime and middleware.
Private cloud is a deployment model, not a service type.

questions.explanation: PaaS abstracts the OS and platform so developers focus on code and data.

questions.question: Which TWO Azure services are examples of PaaS?

options.why: Correct. It is a managed web hosting platform.
Correct. It is a managed database engine.

questions.explanation: App Service and Azure SQL Database are platform services; VMs are IaaS; Microsoft 365 is SaaS.

questions.question: In a PaaS deployment, which of the following remains the customer's responsibility?

options.why: The provider patches the OS in PaaS.
Always the provider's responsibility in public cloud.
Correct. You always own your app and data.

questions.explanation: In PaaS, customers manage applications, data, identities and access. The provider runs the platform.

questions.scenario: A two-person team is building a new web API. They want automatic scaling and do not want to patch servers.
questions.question: Which service type best fits?

options.why: IaaS would require them to patch and scale VMs.
Correct. App Service gives autoscale and no OS patching.
SaaS is finished software; they are building their own API.
That requires buying and running hardware.

questions.explanation: PaaS is ideal for teams who want to build custom apps without managing infrastructure.
